A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Textual Bayes and MHLP work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original accuracy, calibration, abstention, and conformal factuality experiments, together with qualitative examples in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds AIME acceptance diagnostics and QASPER abstention results using semantic entropy.

M1.justification: The Bayesian prompt formulation, TextGrad proposals, MH acceptance rule, approximation scheme, and factuality surrogate remain unchanged. Appendix A.2 and Algorithm 2 document the existing TextGrad update; the added inference equation restates the existing posterior-predictive sampling procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use AIME 2024, SimpleQA, QASPER, and FactScore biographies, including the same missing-context and random-context QASPER scenarios. The new appendix analyses reuse existing AIME and QASPER coverage.

E2.justification: Paraphrasing, System-Message, CoT, and TextGrad remain the uncertainty-comparison baselines; fixed-prompt GPT-4 frequency scoring remains the factuality comparator. Table 11 applies semantic entropy to the same methods rather than introducing additional comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix B.4 adds an evaluation using semantic entropy instead of confidence as the abstention score for QASPER without context, retaining ROC AUC. Existing sample counts, models, chain lengths, burn-in, thinning, and hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds focused AIME acceptance-rate diagnostics and example accept/reject decisions in Figure 3 and Table 10, plus an uncertainty-score robustness check in Appendix B.4. The original SimpleQA and QASPER case studies are retained.

E5.justification: The stated ten-run standard-error reporting and 1,000-split factuality standard deviations are unchanged. New Figure 3 contains a shaded acceptance-rate band without defining its meaning or estimation procedure, preventing a reliable determination of whether it introduces a different uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3, Figure 2, and the original example counts are unchanged. New Table 11 reports semantic-entropy abstention AUCs, including MHLP at 78.2 ± 1.1% and CoT at 71.3 ± 1.8%; these use a different scoring condition from Table 3. Figure 3 and Table 10 add acceptance observations.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 corrects the general hot-posterior criterion from beta < n to beta < n/b and correctly identifies the sum of token log-probabilities as log p rather than p. The underlying Bayesian, MH, and conformal mathematics is otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The title now specifies prompt uncertainty. The introduction narrows the novelty claim from first quantifying prompt uncertainty and performing Bayesian inference over free-form textual variables to first performing Bayesian inference over free-form prompts in LLM-based systems. The four principal contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the QASPER out-of-distribution-generalization framing with detecting insufficient information. It adds interpretations connecting acceptance rates to the 0.234 heuristic and supporting robustness to semantic entropy. Its claim that relative performances match is broader than the tables support: MHLP remains first, but baseline rankings change.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds a feedback-prompt example, TextGrad pseudocode, and clarification of the open-source optimizer step. A new reproducibility statement supplies a repository URL. These expand documentation rather than establish implementation changes; Algorithm 2 does contain a loss-argument ordering inconsistency with Equation 17.

R1.justification: v2 adds related uncertainty literature, including Bayesian Prompt Ensembles, BIRD, and further prompt-based uncertainty methods, plus Gelman et al. for the acceptance-rate interpretation. This modestly broadens the literature coverage alongside the narrower introduction novelty claim.

P1.justification: v2 polishes prose, updates the title and contact information, adopts author-year citations, and expands the method summary. The tempering discussion moves into Appendix A.1, and Appendix A.2 adds implementation explanation. The main section sequence and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adopts ICLR formatting, relocates Figure 1, adjusts table placement, and reformats and captions the existing example tables as Tables 6–9. Algorithm 2, Figure 3, and Tables 10–11 are added; the original principal figures and tables retain their content.

improvement.justification: The added implementation guidance, repository link, and narrower novelty claim improve clarity and reproducibility information. Table 11 also supports MHLP's lead under another uncertainty score. These are limited gains: the principal evidence is unchanged, and new material includes an inconsistent loss-argument order, an undefined diagnostic band, and overstated baseline-ranking consistency.
